Restored to the bytes the .201 dev lane actually applied (content sha c1691130, commit 559ee461a, applied 2026-08-22 20:09:18+00). Commit 7de798a4a had rewritten this applied file in place with 46 lines of reconciliation and five SET NOT NULL that no database ever ran. The delta is re-expressed additively in 0002, minus name/provider which 0001 deliberately relaxes.

CI shape reconciliation requires 0000 to include explicit ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS guards after CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; the same idempotent reconciliation is expressed additively in 0001 for already-applied deployments.

Both 0000 and 0001 spelled every declared-NOT-NULL column as `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS <col> <type> NOT NULL`, which cannot reconcile a drifted table that holds rows: PostgreSQL raises 'column "<col>" of relation "<t>" contains null values' and ON_ERROR_STOP=1 kills the Job -- the same deploy-stopping failure the reconciliation exists to prevent, so tests/ci/test_node_migration_shape_reconciliation.py went GREEN while the failure class stayed open. Proven by execution on the .201 dev lane 2026-08-28 against a seeded drifted consumer_flow_windows (only consumer_group, one row): the NOT NULL spelling exits 3 on `topic`; the nullable spelling exits 0 and converges all 14 columns. Rewriting both files is safe because neither was ever applied -- to_regclass() for both relations is ABSENT on the .201 dev lane, so no content_sha256 is recorded anywhere to conflict with. The applied-ness question is settled only by platform_catalog.schema_migrations; probe it with scripts/migrations/check_migration_applied_on_lane.py. The conclusion above stands on the to_regclass() evidence that precedes the struck clause.] The corrected delta is re-expressed additively in 0002.

0001 shipped an internal LAN address in a header comment. omnimarket blocks that literal (leaked-literals gate OMN-10580) while its node-migration-vendor-parity-gate requires the omnimarket source file to be byte-identical to this vendored copy, so the address cannot be scrubbed on one side only. The scrub is COMMENT-ONLY -- every executable statement in 0001 is byte-unchanged -- and the recorded content_sha256 is updated with it. CORRECTED OMN-17139: the safety claim originally recorded here was false. It read '0001 has only ever been applied by hand (psql -f) ... never through run-forward-migrations.sh, so no onex_application_migration_manifest row records its prior checksum on any lane.' Both halves fail. The dev lane applied 0001 THROUGH run-forward-migrations.sh at 2026-08-30 04:59:57Z and recorded it in platform_catalog.schema_migrations (checksum cba8013e..., provenance file:nodes/node_projection_work_events/0001_create_work_events.sql) -- two hours before this rewrite merged. And onex_application_migration_manifest is not the relation that gates: it is a TEMP table bootstrap.sql builds from the checked-in TSV, so a to_regclass() probe against it reads clean on every lane and proves nothing. The gate is migration_is_applied() in run-forward-migrations.sh, reading platform_catalog.schema_migrations; it hard-failed the dev lane at dev tip. The rewrite itself is genuinely comment-only (every executable statement byte-unchanged, proven by scripts/migrations/prove_migration_revision_equivalence.py) and is admitted by the declaration in _ledger/verified-canonical-adoptions.tsv, not by this row. The successor named here additionally closes a real gap -- summary is bounded at 2000 chars in ModelWorkEventRow but the column was bare TEXT.

0031 resolved tenant identity from a CLOSED THREE-VALUE LITERAL CASE with no ELSE. The live table holds 169 rows across SIX writing slugs (census 2026-08-29), nine of them outside that map -- including one belonging to a real, active, externally-owned customer provisioned eight days AFTER 0031 was authored (that customer's slug was quoted here verbatim until OMN-17288 removed it: this repository is PUBLIC and the identifier was a live one). The map is incomplete BY CONSTRUCTION: omninode_cloud.public.tenants grows on every beta signup (39 tenants and counting), and a migration is immutable once applied, so no literal map authored at any point in time can stay correct. 0031's bytes CANNOT be revised. The .201 dev lane's platform_catalog.schema_migrations holds it with checksum 79ee3b021d0a04088b2f733fa0558ea110b2a6f75b4fb338abe9c5c123f74442 kind content_sha256, byte-identical to both committed copies and to this ledger's own manifest row; bootstrap.sql raises 'conflicting migration checksum in canonical node history' on any divergence (the OMN-16705 class). Four-lane sweep 2026-08-29: dev PRESENT and column already uuid, stability-test absent and column still text, prod and judge carry no platform_catalog ledger at all. 0032 re-expresses the conversion additively and resolves identity by JOINing tenant_registry_mirror -- a runtime-populated relation fed by node_projection_tenant_registry from onex.tenant.events -- instead of inlining any literal. No slug appears in its transform expression. It is a no-op on the dev lane (column already uuid) and fail-closed everywhere else: an unresolvable slug aborts, naming the slugs and stating that the projection has not caught up. Operator ruling 2026-08-29, verbatim: 'Hold + fix mechanism'. BOTH 0031 and 0032 remain in the OMN-15349 fence baseline until the operator un-gates.

0032 put three statements AFTER its DO block -- DROP POLICY / CREATE POLICY / GRANT SELECT on delegation_events. Two defects follow from that one shape, both proven against 0032's real bytes on a scratch Postgres in omnimarket tests/test_omn17288_migration_policy_atomicity.py rather than argued. (a) THE DOCUMENTED NO-OP PATH ABORTED: RETURN exits the DO block, not the file, so on a lane without delegation_events those three statements still ran and raised 'relation "delegation_events" does not exist' -- the one path 0032 described as 'nothing to convert' was the one path that could not complete. (b) RLS ENABLED WITH ZERO POLICIES BETWEEN TRANSACTIONS: the runner is psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f <file> with NO --single-transaction (0032 says so itself), so END$$ COMMITS with tenant_isolation dropped and the policy is only recreated by the standalone statement after it; an interruption in that window leaves a FORCE-RLS table with no policy at all, denying every application read until someone re-runs. 0033 moves the policy recreate and the app_dashboard GRANT INSIDE the guarded DO block, so the drop and the recreate share one transaction, and makes the already-uuid branch fall through to that restatement instead of RETURNing past it. Nothing follows END$$, so the table-absent RETURN is a no-op in fact and not only in prose. The identity mechanism is carried over verbatim: no literal slug in the resolution path, identity resolved by JOINing tenant_registry_mirror, fail-closed pre-guard naming the projection. The whole pre-existing OMN-16930 replay (omnimarket tests/test_omn16930_conversion_replay.py, 9 tests) passes unchanged against 0033. 0032's bytes are NOT applied on any lane -- probed read-only 2026-08-31 against platform_catalog.schema_migrations on all four .201 lanes: dev holds 0030+0031 and NOT 0032, stability-test holds 0030 and NOT 0032, prod and judge carry no platform_catalog ledger at all. Superseded rather than edited anyway, on two independent grounds: check_migration_append_only.py refuses any modification to a manifest-declared file without a higher-ordinal successor landed in the same diff, and check_migration_applied_on_lane.py treats prod/judge's absent ledger as NO_LEDGER, which it exits non-zero on by design because an indeterminate probe is not a negative answer. This row also authorises the one other edit to 0032 in this change: a prose comment quoted a live customer's tenant slug in a PUBLIC repo (OMN-17288 finding 2) and it is removed. 0031, 0032 and 0033 ALL remain in the OMN-15349 fence baseline until the operator un-gates; when that happens, un-gate 0033 and leave 0031 and 0032 fenced.

0003 drops tenant_isolation INSIDE its DO block (line 127) and recreates it in a standalone statement AFTER END$$ (lines 163-164) -- byte-identical in shape to the 0032 defect OMN-17288 superseded with 0033. The forward runner is `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f <file>` with NO --single-transaction, so END$$ COMMITS: between that commit and the standalone CREATE POLICY, public.capability_scores is ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with zero policies, which denies every row to every non-owner non-BYPASSRLS principal and surfaces as SQLSTATE 42501 -- indistinguishable at the call site from a missing GRANT. This is the THIRD instance of the class and the FIRST one that actually ran: unlike 0032 (applied on no lane), 0003 is recorded in the .201 dev lane's platform_catalog.schema_migrations, applied 2026-08-17 02:30:59.157734+00 (read-only probe as `postgres`, 2026-08-31). The window was traversed on a real database and was not interrupted; live readback the same day shows relrowsecurity=t, relforcerowsecurity=t and exactly one policy, so 0004 is a window closure and a convergence, not a repair of observed damage. Found by scripts/validation/check_migration_rls_policy_atomicity.py RULE B (added by OMN-17298) on its first run against the checked-in tree -- not by review. 0003's bytes are NOT edited by this change: it is applied with a recorded content_sha256, so an in-place edit would raise 'conflicting migration checksum in canonical node history' on the dev lane (the OMN-16705 class), and check_migration_append_only.py refuses it independently. 0004 restates the policy and the OMN-14894 app_dashboard GRANT inside one guarded DO block with nothing following it, carrying 0003's predicate over verbatim including the ::uuid cast. It deliberately does not re-express the tenant_id TEXT->UUID conversion, which is 0003's and is idempotent there.
